prov.text: The increase in net income during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 reflected growth in net interest income and noninterest income, which more than offset higher levels of noninterest expense, federal income tax expense, and provision for credit losses expense. The improved net income during the first nine months of 2026 compared to the respective 2025 period reflected increases in net interest income and noninterest income and lower provision for credit losses expense, which more than offset larger noninterest expense and federal income tax expense. Net interest income increased during the 2026 periods due to earning asset expansion and decreases in the costs of funds, which outweighed lower yields on earning assets and growth in interest-bearing liabilities. The growth in noninterest income during the 2026 periods mainly resulted from increased treasury management fees, largely reflecting customers’ expanded use of products and services and new client acquisitions.

nonint.text: This report contains certain non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted net income, adjusted noninterest expense, and adjusted diluted earnings per share, each of which excludes after-tax costs associated with (i) Mercantile’s acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation ("Eastern Michigan") that was completed during the fourth quarter of 2025 ($0.2 million and $0.5 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively) , and (ii) the previously announced core and digital banking system conversions ($0.4 million and $3.9 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively). These non-GAAP financial measures are identified in this report where they appear. We believe that presenting these non-GAAP financial measures provides investors, analysts, and other interested parties with meaningful supplementary information to assess Mercantile’s underlying operational performance by removing the effect of costs we consider to be non-recurring in nature and not reflective of Mercantile’s core operating results. These non-GAAP financial measures are used by management to evaluate Mercantile’s ongoing operations, for internal planning and forecasting purposes, and to assess period-over-period comparability. Management believes it is useful for the reader to review these non-GAAP adjusted measures alongside the GAAP measures.

We believe that presenting these non-GAAP financial measures provides investors, analysts, and other interested parties with meaningful supplementary information to assess Mercantile’s underlying operational performance by removing the effect of costs we consider to be non-recurring in nature and not reflective of Mercantile’s core operating results. pretax.text: During the third quarter of 2026, we recorded income before federal income tax of $29.0 million and federal income tax expense of $4.9 million. During the third quarter of 2025, we recorded income before federal income tax of $27.5 million and federal income tax expense of $3.7 million. During the first nine months of 2026, we recorded income before federal income tax of $87.4 million and federal income tax expense of $14.7 million. During the first nine months of 2025, we recorded income before federal income tax of $77.4 million and federal income tax expense of $11.5 million. The increases in federal income tax expense during the 2026 periods mainly resulted from higher levels of income before federal income tax and lower levels of net benefits from transferable energy tax credits. The acquisition of transferable energy tax credits and the net benefits from low-income housing and historic tax credit investments provided for aggregate tax benefits of $0.8 million and $1.7 million during the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $2.4 million and $3.6 million during the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively. The recording of the tax benefits positively impacted our effective tax rate, which equaled 16.8% and 13.4% during the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively, and 16.8% and 14.9% during the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

net.text: This report contains certain non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted net income, adjusted noninterest expense, and adjusted diluted earnings per share, each of which excludes after-tax costs associated with (i) Mercantile’s acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation ("Eastern Michigan") that was completed during the fourth quarter of 2025 ($0.2 million and $0.5 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively) , and (ii) the previously announced core and digital banking system conversions ($0.4 million and $3.9 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively). These non-GAAP financial measures are identified in this report where they appear. We believe that presenting these non-GAAP financial measures provides investors, analysts, and other interested parties with meaningful supplementary information to assess Mercantile’s underlying operational performance by removing the effect of costs we consider to be non-recurring in nature and not reflective of Mercantile’s core operating results. These non-GAAP financial measures are used by management to evaluate Mercantile’s ongoing operations, for internal planning and forecasting purposes, and to assess period-over-period comparability. Management believes it is useful for the reader to review these non-GAAP adjusted measures alongside the GAAP measures.

Net interest income.text: Net interest income grew $8.9 million and $24.0 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, compared to the same prior-year time periods, reflecting the combined impact of $4.6 million and $14.5 million increases in interest income and $4.3 million and $9.6 million reductions in interest expense during the respective time periods. Our net interest margin during the third quarter of 2026 was 24 basis points higher than during the third quarter of 2025 and was 14 basis points higher during the first nine months of 2026 compared to the first nine months of 2025. Although our yield on earning assets declined during the 2026 time periods compared to the respective 2025 time periods, largely reflecting the aggregate 75 basis point reduction in the federal funds rate during the last four months of 2025, our cost of funds declined by a larger amount primarily due to the decline in the interest rate environment and the onboarding of Eastern Michigan Bank’s relatively low-cost deposit base. Growth in earning assets also contributed to the higher level of net interest income. Average earning assets during the first nine months of 2026 totaled $6.46 billion, compared to $5.79 billion during the first nine months of 2025.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income totaled $12.3 million and $35.4 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, compared to $10.4 million and $30.6 million during the respective time periods in 2025. We recorded strong growth in treasury management fees and payroll service fees, along with improved interest rate swap income. Eastern Michigan Bank’s noninterest income totaled $0.5 million and $1.6 million during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively.

intro.text: Based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Mercantile Bank Corporation is the bank holding company for Mercantile Bank and Eastern Michigan Bank. Mercantile Bank and Eastern Michigan Bank provide financial products and services in a professional and personalized manner designed to make banking easier for businesses, individuals, and governmental units. Distinguished by exceptional service, knowledgeable staff, and a commitment to the communities they serve, Mercantile Bank and Eastern Michigan Bank together comprise one of the largest Michigan-based banking organizations with total combined assets of approximately $6.8 billion. Mercantile Bank Corporation's common stock is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol "MBWM." For more information about Mercantile, visit www.mercbank.com, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X (formerly Twitter) @MercBank, and LinkedIn @merc-bank.
